# rust-skia Bindings & Wrappers

How to add or update the C++↔Rust boundary of rust-skia: the `extern "C"` shims in
`skia-bindings/src/*.cpp` and the safe wrappers in `skia-safe/src/**`.

This skill is the single source of truth for binding and wrapper mechanics. The
milestone-update skill, `AGENTS.md`, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` refer
here instead of restating the rules.

## When to Use

- Adding a missing binding or wrapper for a Skia API.
- A Skia header changed and the existing wrapper must follow.
- Deciding whether an accessor needs a C shim or can use direct field access.
- Reviewing a binding PR for layout, ownership, `Send`/`Sync`, and naming.

## Reference Files

- [`references/c-shims.md`](references/c-shims.md) — the C++ side: file wiring, naming
  conventions, `sk_sp`/`unique_ptr`/`optional` idioms, callbacks, anchor functions.
- [`references/wrapper-kinds.md`](references/wrapper-kinds.md) — the Rust side: which
  wrapper kind to pick, traits, `Debug`, `Send`/`Sync`, strings, slices, tests.
- [`references/exceptions.md`](references/exceptions.md) — when the normal pattern does
  **not** apply, and how to recognise those cases.

## Procedure

### 1. Read the C++ API and its neighbours

Read the full header, not just the declaration you need. Skia's types are
interconnected: a new method often returns a type that needs its own decision, and
the enclosing class determines the wrapper kind. Also read the existing wrapper for
the same class if one exists — extending it is usually the whole task.

### 2. Decide whether a C shim is needed at all

Work down this list and stop at the first match:

| C++ API | Action |
|---|---|
| Public data member of a C-compatible type, generated by bindgen | **No shim.** Read/write `self.native().fFoo` / `self.native_mut().fFoo` directly. |
| Member function whose parameters **and** return value are all C-compatible types | **No shim.** Call it on `self.native()` / `self.native_mut()`. |
| Smart-pointer return (`sk_sp<T>`, `unique_ptr<T>`) | **Shim**, returning the released raw pointer. |
| Return value that is not trivially relocatable, or `SkSpan`/`std::optional`/`std::string_view` parameter | **Shim** with an out-parameter or a `(ptr, len)` pair. |
| Non-trivial constructor/destructor | **Shim**: placement `new` + explicit `~T()` call. |
| Virtual interface to be implemented in Rust | **Shim**: a C++ adapter class plus a function-pointer table. |
| Overloads bindgen cannot disambiguate, or a type only reachable through the API | **Shim** (or an anchor function). |

"Call it directly" is only safe when *every* parameter **and** the return value are
C-compatible — that is, types bindgen can represent in Rust and that can cross an
`extern "C"` boundary by value or by pointer. A single non-C-compatible parameter or
return type (a smart pointer, a `std` container, an opaque type, a wrong layout)
forces a shim for the whole function. A merely non-`const` parameter does not: supply
it with `native_mut_force()`.

Direct field access is preferred over getter/setter shims. `bindgen` keeps the `f`
prefix, so a field is `fUseDrawListLayer` on the Rust side. Confirm the field is
actually generated — look for the `offset_of!` assert next to the struct in the
generated bindings — before relying on it.

```rust
pub fn use_draw_list_layer(&self) -> bool {
    self.native().fUseDrawListLayer
}

pub fn set_use_draw_list_layer(&mut self, use_draw_list_layer: bool) -> &mut Self {
    self.native_mut().fUseDrawListLayer = use_draw_list_layer;
    self
}
```

### 3. Write the C shim

Add it to the feature-gated `.cpp` file that owns the header, following the naming
convention `C_<Scope>_<name>` (`_Construct`, `_CopyConstruct`, `_destruct`, `_new`,
`_delete`, `_Make*`, `_Types`). Static functions and factories begin with an
uppercase letter, member methods with a lowercase one. Preserve the original C++
casing of the method name.

A **new** `.cpp` file must be added to `binding_sources` in
`skia-bindings/build_support/skia_bindgen.rs` under the right feature gate, or it is
neither compiled nor parsed. That list is the only authoritative source list; there is
no build file to keep in sync.

Document any non-obvious ownership or lifetime decision in a C++ comment at the shim
— that comment is the only place the reasoning is visible to a future reader. See
[`references/exceptions.md`](references/exceptions.md) for the established rationale
comments worth imitating.

### 4. Regenerate and check

```sh
touch skia-bindings/src/bindings.cpp && cargo check -p skia-bindings
```

Bindgen is re-run when any `src/*.cpp` or the Skia `include/` directory changes.
The output lands in `target/*/build/skia-bindings-*/out/skia/bindings.rs`;
`make locate-bindings` prints the newest one and `make open-bindings` opens it.
Read the generated bindings to confirm names, signatures, and field presence before
writing the Rust wrapper. The bindings are feature-dependent, so check with the same
features you intend to test.

### 5. Write the Rust wrapper

Pick the wrapper kind from
[`references/wrapper-kinds.md`](references/wrapper-kinds.md), implement the traits
the kind requires (`NativeDrop`, `NativeRefCountedBase`, …), add `Debug`, decide
`Send`/`Sync` deliberately, and add a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block in the same
file. Port the C++ documentation following the `cpp-to-rust-documentation` skill.

### 6. Verify

- `cargo check -p skia-safe` with the relevant features, plus the full feature set
  used by CI if the change touches a shared file.
- The in-file tests, and `skia-safe/tests/send_sync.rs` when `Send`/`Sync` changed.
- For wrapper changes, the public API diff: `make diff-api`.
- Re-read the C++ header and the Rust file side by side to confirm ordering parity
  of top-level types, nested types, methods, and debug fields.

## Style & Conventions

See `AGENTS.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` for the full set. Highlights:

- Keep Rust method and debug-field ordering aligned with the upstream C++ header order.
- Keep top-level type declarations in the same sequence as the upstream C++ header, and
  define nested Rust types directly below their parent.
- Derive `Debug` for all public types unless there is a specific reason not to; place
  `Debug` first in the derive list.
- Access bindgen-generated fields of C-compatible types directly; do not wrap public
  data members in C getter/setter functions.
- Do not pass C++ class types by value across `extern "C"`; use pointers and/or
  out-parameters. Use placement new for non-trivial out-parameters.
- Use `pub` visibility by default; `pub(crate)` only inside an already crate-public module.
- Write one `use` line per module; do not group several modules into one `use` tree.
  A list of items of a single module (`use std::io::{self, Cursor};`) is fine.
- Only comment to explain non-obvious reasoning or intent.
